scheme_name: PMMSY: Construction of New Rearing ponds - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on May 20, 2020. 

This scheme aims to promote sustainable and responsible development of the fisheries sector in India. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive scheme that encompasses various aspects of the fisheries sector including aquaculture, marine fisheries, and post-harvest management. 

The specific initiative of constructing new rearing ponds falls under the umbrella of PMMSY. 

The objective of this initiative is to enhance fish production and productivity in the state of Haryana. 

The scheme aims to increase fish production in the state by 70 percent by the year 2024. 

This target translates to an increase in fish production from approximately 1.5 lakh metric tons to about 2.5 lakh metric tons. 

The construction of new rearing ponds is intended to provide a controlled environment for fish breeding and rearing. 

These ponds will facilitate the cultivation of various fish species which are in high demand in local and national markets. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is substantial. 

Farmers can receive up to 60 percent of the project cost as a subsidy for constructing new rearing ponds. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, this subsidy can go up to 80 percent of the project cost. 

The maximum subsidy amount for constructing a new rearing pond is capped at INR 10 lakh. 

This means that a farmer can potentially receive a subsidy of up to INR 8 lakh if they belong to SC or ST categories. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specific and well-defined. 

Applicants must be residents of Haryana and should possess a valid identity proof. 

Farmers must be engaged in fish farming or have a genuine interest in starting fish farming. 

There are no strict educational qualifications required for applicants. 

However, they must demonstrate knowledge of fish farming practices or be willing to undergo training. 

The application process for the construction of new rearing ponds is straightforward. 

Interested applicants must visit the official website of the Department of Fisheries, Haryana. 

They can download the application form from the website or obtain it from the local fisheries office. 

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents. 

These documents include identity proof, land ownership documents, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local fisheries department. 

The department will conduct a site inspection to verify the details provided in the application. 

If the application is approved, the subsidy will be disbursed in installments. 

The first installment will be released after the construction of the pond begins. 

The second installment will be released upon the completion of the pond. 

The entire process from application submission to subsidy disbursement typically takes about three to six months. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Fisheries, Government of Haryana. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the implementation of PMMSY in the state. 

They provide technical assistance and guidance to farmers throughout the process. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries can be found on their official website. 

Farmers can also reach out to local fisheries officers for any queries related to the scheme. 

In addition to constructing new rearing ponds, PMMSY also focuses on enhancing the quality of fish seed and feed. 

The scheme promotes the establishment of hatcheries and feed mills to support fish farming. 

This holistic approach aims to create a sustainable ecosystem for fish farming in Haryana. 

The state government has allocated a budget of INR 20 crores for the implementation of PMMSY in Haryana for the financial year 2021-2022. 

This budget is aimed at supporting various initiatives under the scheme including the construction of new rearing ponds. 

The PMMSY initiative is expected to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

It is estimated that the scheme will generate around 10,000 direct and indirect jobs in Haryana. 

The scheme also aims to empower women by promoting their participation in fish farming. 

Women are encouraged to take up fish farming as a viable source of income. 

The PMMSY initiative aligns with the Government of India’s vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It also supports the goal of achieving self-sufficiency in fish production in the country. 

The scheme is part of a larger effort to promote sustainable agriculture and rural development. 

The construction of new rearing ponds is expected to improve the livelihoods of many farmers in Haryana. 

By increasing fish production, the scheme will also contribute to food security in the state. 

The PMMSY initiative is a significant step towards modernizing the fisheries sector in India. 

It aims to adopt scientific practices in fish farming to enhance productivity. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable practices to protect aquatic ecosystems. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt eco-friendly methods in their fish farming practices. 

The PMMSY initiative is expected to have a positive impact on the economy of Haryana. 

By boosting fish production, it will contribute to the overall growth of the agricultural sector. 

The scheme is also expected to enhance the nutritional intake of the local population. 

Fish is a rich source of protein and essential nutrients. 

The PMMSY initiative is a comprehensive approach to transforming the fisheries sector in Haryana. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable fish farming ecosystem. 

The construction of new rearing ponds is a crucial component of this transformation. 

The scheme is expected to benefit thousands of farmers across the state. 

The PMMSY initiative represents a significant investment in the future of fisheries in India. 

It aims to create a vibrant and sustainable fisheries sector that can support the livelihoods of millions. 

The success of this initiative will depend on the active participation of farmers and stakeholders. 

The government is committed to providing the necessary support and resources to ensure the success of the PMMSY initiative.
